ravi: quick heads-up: onboarding run for `orion-lite-6b-int4a` on staging (32k ctx) shows reproducible jitter and occasional token reorder exactly at the 4096->8192 boundary during long-prefill. filing here before i open a MR.

clare: reorder? can you paste the smallest repro + a short log snippet?

ravi: repro command: `python tests/long_prefill.py --model orion-lite-6b-int4a --prefill 9000 --seed 13 --log-level debug`

niko: logs:
```
[2025-11-07T08:02:01Z] prefill.start id=pf-e2b9 tokens=9000 model=orion-lite-6b-int4a
[2025-11-07T08:02:05Z] kvcache.append shard=0 window=4096->8192 page_size=4096 page_hash=fa34d2
[2025-11-07T08:02:06Z] warning: rope.rescale_jump window=4096 old_scale=1.0 new_scale=0.9987
[2025-11-07T08:02:06Z] decode.token 4089 tok=it prob=0.45
[2025-11-07T08:02:07Z] decode.token 4106 tok=it prob=0.03  <-- reordered/low-prob divergence
[2025-11-07T08:02:07Z] kvcache.handshake prefill_id=pf-e2b9 page_hash=fa34d2 ok
```

clare: interesting — rope.rescale_jump logged at same moment. does this reproduce with fp16/int8?

ravi: quick matrix locally: fp16/rescale=true -> clean; int8/rescale=true -> infrequent minor jitter; int4a/rescale=true -> consistent reorder at boundary.

quant-lab-bot: analysis hint: int4a kernel uses 4-bit pack stride=16, known sensitivity when buffer copy boundary == page_size. Refer to ticket QLAB-412.

niko: two hypotheses: (A) rescale path mutates token offsets while page commit is in-flight causing transient consumer read of partially-updated KV page, (B) int4a packing/unpacking plus memcpy ordering yields reordering when page boundary aligns with pack stride.

clare: can you rerun with `--enable_rope_rescale=false` and `--kvcache-sync-commit=true` to isolate? also try `--kvcache-page-size=2048`.

ravi: rerun commands i used:
```
# A: baseline
python tests/long_prefill.py --model orion-lite-6b-int4a --prefill 9000 --seed 13 --log-level debug
# B: rescale off
python tests/long_prefill.py --model orion-lite-6b-int4a --prefill 9000 --seed 13 --enable_rope_rescale=false --log-level debug
# C: sync commits
python tests/long_prefill.py --model orion-lite-6b-int4a --prefill 9000 --seed 13 --kvcache_sync_commit=true --log-level debug
# D: small page
python tests/long_prefill.py --model orion-lite-6b-int4a --prefill 9000 --seed 13 --kvcache_page_size=2048 --log-level debug
```

ravi: results summary: B (rescale=false) eliminates reorder on 6/6 runs; C reduces frequency to 1/6; D reduces frequency but still occasional. suggests rescale is a big factor.

niko: can you attach token-diff CSV for 4070-4120 around the boundary with rescale on/off? we need spectral comparison to see whether tokens flip order or probabilities shift then decoder chooses different token.

ravi: generated diffs and uploaded to ci: https://ci.internal/artifacts/longprefill/1769998001/diffs.zip

ops-bot: staged sweep queued: job=staging-longprefill-3421 variants=[fp16,int8,int4a] runs=8 flags=[KV_LOG_EXTRA=1,ROPE_RESCALE_DEBUG=1,KVCACHE_PAGE_HASH_VERBOSE=1] requested_by=ravi

clare: if this is rescale+quant amplification, short term mitigation: disable rope rescale during prefill for onboarding quant models and add a boundary-check to the model-onboard smoke (check at 4k,8k,16k). we need a PR to gate rescale behind `--allow_prefill_rescale` and default off for quant.

quant-lab-bot: workaround patch available: refs/heads/qlab/safe-rescale-guard — includes a conservative threshold and extra stability checks. performance cost ~1.8% at longer sequences.

niko: long term we should make rescale idempotent w.r.t. in-flight page commits and add sequence numbers to page headers (so consumer can detect and ignore partial updates). also audit memcpy ordering in int4a unpack path.

ci-bot: job 3421 scheduled. artifacts will be at https://ci.internal/reports/3421/

ravi: i'll open MR with failing trace, diffs, and a short benchmark comparing rescale on/off for fp16/int8/int4a. cc @clare @niko for review.

clare: thanks — add onboarding checklist item if MR confirms. also please include a quick perf table so product understands impact. :thumbsup:
